summary:
This is a stale re-validation at e990514. Between a3d3860, which I validated last time, and HEAD, the only non-record change is the O-025 fix: docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md, lines 17-19. `git diff --name-only a3d3860 HEAD -- src tests eng` is empty. Nothing is mid-merge, and 2e089a1 (uat, which brings in SL-040) is an ancestor of HEAD.

**Build and tests**
- Clean Release rebuild (--no-incremental): 0 warnings, 0 errors, and the DLLs are fresh.
- Full Core.Tests: 199 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. That includes ScanStoreRollupTests (17), HardlinkTests (5), LinkTests, UnreadableFolderTests, TopLevelTests (15), ArchitectureRulesTests (8), RuleCopiesAgree, and SL-040's LargestFiles tests (9 + scale).
- Timing: 10 reads of a 100,000-child folder took 8.73–12.01 ms, against a 250 ms limit.
- 5M-entry memory budget: 652.1 MiB retained, 670.3 MiB peak, against 800 MiB (GC heap, not private bytes).
- Fitness: all 32 rules hold.

**O-025**
The amended doc line matches ScanStore.Charges (ScanStore.cs:275-276), which charges only a File that is not flagged HardlinkDuplicate.

**Real data**
I ran a throwaway probe against the freshly built Core DLL (hash matched). It scans through the real Scanner, and its oracles don't use the store's own rules: its own first-seen dedup over the listed IDs, its own charge rule over raw sizes read by reflection, its own bottom-up sums, and its own ordering and share check.
- **C:\Windows, three scans:** each scan found 0 dedup disagreements (54,992 later names), 0 charge disagreements, 0 rollup mismatches in 157,748 folders, and 0 bad ordered reads. Root equals Totals, which equals the sum of the top-level rows. The slowest single read was 16.74 ms.
- **Repeatability (new evidence):** the three scans gave identical totals in every folder and the same 54,992 duplicate names. WinSxS was 9,966,250,576 B on disk every time. This is the tree where the spike measured 68 folders swinging by more than 10 MiB with 16 workers, so the design's single-writer rule makes first-seen charging repeatable on it.
- **C:\Program Files, two scans (30 links, 2 unreadable folders):** the same checks found 0 mismatches, and the totals match the last validation to the byte (34,100,818,396 / 34,154,406,672 / 77,391).

**Published app**
- I published the single-file exe and ran it twice on C:\Windows through eng/read-window.ps1: exit 0 and Completed both times. In each run the top-level rows sum to the core totals.
- The project's window cases passed all 26 non-network cases, including C-003 (a hardlinked pair counted once through the window) and SL-040's B-001 to B-008.

**Not checked**
The real-NTFS half of case 8 again could not be produced: 0 of 168,189 real folders state a non-zero size of their own.

**The slice's shape**
Builds 2 and 3 were both sent back from the merge, and build 3 changed no src. The attempt-3 objection said the branch held only first-attempt records. That was literally true of the committed tree at a3d3860: `git ls-tree` shows only the -1 records. e990514 commits the -2 records, but build-slice-3.json and code-review-3.json are still untracked. If the merge again judges by the records committed on the branch, this becomes a third lap with no code change. That is a record-commit issue, not a code issue.

The worktree was left as found, and the temp probe and publish output were removed.

criteria.criterion: 1. C1: chain 10,000 folders deep, one file per level
criteria.how: AChainTenThousandFoldersDeepRollsEveryFileUpToEveryAncestor passed in my Release run at e990514.

criteria.criterion: 2. C1: one folder with 100,000 direct children, 1,000 of them subfolders holding files
3. C1: empty, nested empty, empty root, seeded mixed tree, oracle after every append
criteria.how: EmptyAndMixedTreesMatchTheOracleAtEveryCut passed. On real data an independent bottom-up oracle over raw sizes matched all 157,748 + 10,441 folders, in every run.

criteria.criterion: 4. C2, C3: one ID under three names in three folders, fixed order
criteria.how: OneIdUnderThreeNamesInThreeFoldersIsChargedOnceToTheFirstNamesFolder passed. On real data the store's flag agreed with an independent first-seen dedup on every file (54,992 and 224 later names), and the choice of first holder was identical across repeated scans.

criteria.criterion: 5. C2, C3: names sharing an ancestor or a parent
6. C2: IDs that must not match (0, all-ones, widened 64-bit all-ones, same low half)
criteria.how: IdsThatMustNotMatchAreEachCharged passed. The code is unchanged since the last validation.

criteria.criterion: 7. C4: a link (5000/8192) and an Unreadable folder (4096/4096) as leaves; appends under a File, Link or Unreadable folder throw
criteria.how: ALinkAndAnUnreadableFolderAreLeavesThatAddNothing, LinkTests and UnreadableFolderTests passed. On real Program Files (30 links, 2 unreadable) the rollups matched the oracle, which charges every non-file 0.

criteria.criterion: 8a. C1, C4: a synthetic folder stating 4096/4096 adds nothing of it
criteria.how: AFolderThatStatesItsOwnSizeAddsNothingOfIt passed. On real data 0 folders charged anything.

criteria.criterion: 8b. C1, C4: a real NTFS folder owning a directory allocation adds nothing of it
criteria.how: Not built (m7 disposition). The probe found 0 of 168,189 real folders stating any non-zero size of their own, so this machine cannot produce the precondition.

criteria.criterion: 9. C5: mixed children with equal sizes and a hardlink duplicate, read three times
criteria.how: ChildrenAreReadLargestFirstWithEqualSizesInListingOrder passed. On real data the order and the Entry tiebreak were correct in every folder, in every run.

criteria.criterion: 10. C5: shares of 3/4 and 1/4 exact, 1/3 within 1e-12, summing to 1
criteria.how: EachChildsShareIsItsOnDiskBytesOverTheFolders passed. On real data every share equalled OnDisk/parent exactly, and the child sums equalled the parent.

criteria.criterion: 11. C5: a 0-byte parent (empty, only duplicates, online-only) gives 0 shares; a File, Link or Unreadable folder passed as the folder
criteria.how: AFolderWithNothingOnDiskGivesEveryChildAZeroShare passed. No NaN appeared in any real folder.

criteria.criterion: 12. C6: 100,000 children, many ties, 10 reads with the cold one counted, Release
criteria.how: The Release trx StdOut shows 8.73–12.01 ms against 250 ms.

criteria.criterion: 13. C1-C4 through the real Scanner on NTFS temp trees; root == Totals; TopLevelRow == rollup
criteria.how: Every real-tree test passed with AssertChargedBytesAreTheTotals. On real C:\Windows and Program Files, root == Totals == the sum of the top-level rows, both through the probe and in the published exe's report.

criteria.criterion: 14. C1: 5,000,000 entries with the three rollup columns and a 100,000-child folder
criteria.how: Budget test: 652.1 MiB retained, 670.3 MiB peak, against 800 MiB (GC heap, not process private bytes).

planned.evidence: The synthetic brute-force tests (a 10,000-deep chain, a 100,000-wide folder, empty and mixed trees) passed at e990514. On real data an independent bottom-up oracle over raw sizes matched RolledSize, RolledOnDisk and FilesBelow in all 157,748 C:\Windows folders (3 runs) and all 10,441 Program Files folders (2 runs): 0 mismatches.

The three-names test passed. The store's first-seen flag matched the probe's own first-seen dedup on every real file (188,526 and 77,391). Across three C:\Windows scans the duplicate set was identical (54,992/54,992) and no folder total moved, including WinSxS, where the 16-worker spike swung by 587 MiB.
The hardlink tests assert FilesBelow at every level, and they passed. The real FilesBelow matched the oracle, which counts every name including the 54,992 later names, in every folder.
ALinkAndAnUnreadableFolderAreLeavesThatAddNothing, LinkTests and UnreadableFolderTests passed. On real Program Files (30 links, 2 unreadable) the oracle, which charges every non-file 0, matched.
The ordering, stable-tie, hand-computed-share and 0-byte-parent tests passed. ChildrenLargestFirst was correct on all 168,189 real folders in every run, with no NaN.
Release timed test: 10 reads of 100,000 children in 8.73–12.01 ms (limit 250 ms). The slowest real folder read was 16.74 ms.

obligations.evidence: docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:17-19 now reads '0 for `Link`, for `HardlinkDuplicate` entries and, since SL-042, for every `Folder` whatever size it states; `Size`/`OnDisk` for a File that is charged'. That matches ScanStore.cs:275-276 (Charges = File && !HardlinkDuplicate), and the real probe found 0 charge disagreements with that rule.
e990514, Release: 8.73–12.01 ms over 10 reads, the cold first included, against 250 ms.
All real-tree tests passed with the rollup assertions. On real C:\Windows and Program Files, root == Totals == top-level row sums, through the probe and the published exe.
e990514: 652.1 MiB retained, 670.3 MiB peak, against 800 MiB.
The merged LargestFilesScaleTests and LargestFilesTests passed, and window cases B-001..B-008 passed on the published exe.

not_reached: The real-NTFS half of case 8 (a folder that owns a directory allocation) was not checked. 0 of 168,189 real folders on this machine state a non-zero size of their own. A volume that reports folder sizes (the opt-in SMB-LOOPBACK rig or N-001..N-004) was not run.
The process private-bytes peak at 5M entries was not measured against the spike's 1 GiB. The budget test measures GC-heap retained and peak (652.1 / 670.3 MiB) against 800 MiB.
No full-drive scan (about 2.4M files) was run, and no real folder had 100,000 children. The real scans were C:\Windows (346,274 entries) and C:\Program Files (87,862 entries).
Non-NTFS or ID-less volumes (FAT, SMB returning 0 IDs) were not scanned. Only the synthetic tests cover the no-ID sentinels.
Nothing in the window reads ChildrenLargestFirst yet, so the screen's half of the 0.5 s tree budget is unmeasured.

Repeatability was confirmed only for the current single-threaded Scanner (3 identical C:\Windows scans). A parallel Scanner, or reads of the rollups from another thread during a scan, is outside the stated contract and was not tested.
eng/rules-harness/harness.py was not run, because it needs the engine's interpreter.

Whether the merge gate will accept the branch: build-slice-3.json, code-review-3.json and this validation's record are not committed at e990514. The attempt-3 objection ('only first-attempt records on the branch') was true of the committed tree at a3d3860. If the merge again judges the committed records, it may send this slice round a third time with no code change.
